messages.text: Library route still icy by the curb. Want me to start from your side of Michigan Ave instead?
That would help. I want to look at Harold's oak before we go. The wind dropped small branches again.
np. I can drag them to the back after work. Big yard earns its keep in March.
A third of an acre always has something to say. I'll bring the clippers.
I can stop by after Kroger. Do you want me to bring the blue envelope from the kitchen table or leave it alone?
Please bring it. I need the red-white card, the blue card, and the little pharmacy booklet together before I call.
All right. I also saw your ledger open to March. The $800 tax line and $310 benefits line are marked paid.
Good. That keeps the month near $2,400 if the furnace behaves.
Mom, I found another gray file box in the workshop. Tabs say 1099, mower parts, and 1984 receipts. Do you want it upstairs?
I put the gray lint roller in your grocery bag. The one you like for the quilt backing.
Yes, please put it by the dining room table. Those carburetor invoices are probably in date order if the rubber band held.
Thank you. Winston climbed onto the frame again before I had the blue squares pinned.
They are. Your adding-machine tape is still clipped to the side.
Of course he did. Move your needle box first, please. He is too heavy to be delicate.
I want to compare one column before I talk to the Washtenaw woman Thursday. Numbers still settle me.
I slid the box into Harold's nightstand. He went straight there and curled up like he owns that side.
I can bring the lemon bars on the 8th if Sarah is doing scones again. Do you still want twelve place settings?
Yes, twelve should do it. I put the folding chairs by the coat rack so I won't forget.
Good. Also, I found two loose receipts from February in my tote... naturally after you had everything clipped.
Bring them Tuesday. I still have the March envelope open beside the old 1996 binder.
May 2 still works for me to come up from Toledo. Sophie has a hospital skills lab that morning, so she may ride separately if she can get loose.
That is fine. I will make the chicken salad. Tell Caleb I found the orange Bowling Green mug he left here.
He'll laugh. Lily has a track thing that weekend, so it may just be me unless the schedule changes. I'll send the meet time when the school posts it.
Send it along. I still owe Sophie a note about the ring photo she sent.
Walk was good today. You still want me to grab the Free Press sports section from Kroger?
Yes, please. I want the Lakeland box score and the Crisler write-up before I do the crossword.
Got it. Old English D on the front and maize on the back page, looks like your kind of paper.
That will make the coffee taste better.
I found the print you mentioned with the woman in the pink dress facing that big gray house. It is more unsettling than I remembered...
Yes, that one. The empty field does half the talking.
Also, the library disc sale has The Searchers and a two-disc porch-music set with Wildwood Flower on it. Shall I hold them until bridge?
Please do. I can give you the $3 on Tuesday.
Weather app says Saline may get freezing rain tonight. Please let Rob handle the driveway in the morning.
Already left his $40 by the side door. I can wait on the newspaper until the walk looks dull, not shiny.
Good. And use the black-handled one if you step out before Kathy gets there.
It is leaning where I cannot miss it. You sound like your sister.
Looks clear by 8. Back side of the library still ok?
Yes. I will park by the book drop and wait there.
Good. Let's keep it to the small loop today; I have a 9:30 budget call.
That suits me. Bring Cooper's spare bag if you remember.
Do you want me to come over before the 10:00 Zoom and make sure the sound is working? Linda's grant meeting link looks different this month.
That would help. I have the February numbers balanced except for one receipt that printed sideways.
Also, she asked whether you ever filled out the little compensation form they sent around last fall.
No need. I like being able to close the laptop when the rows agree and go make soup.
Library route Monday? They have cones by the east lot. 8 still ok?
Yes, 8 is fine. I may be a few minutes dusty from checking the trays at 7.
ty. Dave asked if your cabbage row is already spoken for by that big crock again.
If the seedlings cooperate. I told him there are only two quart jars left, so he should not dawdle.
Did the Tecumseh call go all right this morning?
Yes, fifteen minutes almost exactly. We found Mrs. Harshbarger's notice in the Adrian paper and she remembered the bakery on Maumee Street.
Good. I put two more forever stamps in your kitchen drawer yesterday, behind the recipe box.
Thank you. I used one for Caleb already and may write Dolores this afternoon if my hand behaves.
Mom, when I come tomorrow, do you want me to take the November medicine bottles to the safe-drop box in Toledo? The one with the big white cap and the pink tablets?
Thank you, but Kathy says the Saline pharmacy takes them. I kept them because that ten-day stretch was such a nuisance and I wanted the names written down.
Okay. Also, did Dr. Levin say anything about the little place on your back from last spring?
Only that it looks tidy. I put a clean Band-Aid on anyway because my blouse rubs there.
Greg's cousin keeps saying those little fruit squares helped his legs after golf. Want me to bring one Saturday, or no?
No, thank you. Your nephew made that same offer in 2020 when my knees were acting up, and I passed then too.
Fair enough. I'll bring the ginger tea you liked instead, and I won't let Greg start a lecture. 🙂
Tea is plenty. I also need to be careful with anything extra because of my morning BP pill.
I should pull in around 10:30 tomorrow if 23 isn't backed up. Do you need anything from Toledo?
No, just yourself. I moved the stack of crossword books off Emma's bed so the room is not a storage closet.
She will laugh at that. She asked if the little desk is still by the window for May.
It is, and I found the lamp she used over Christmas.
Mom, I found the old Woodward Ave. picture with Dad in the Tigers cap. Marco says it belongs in the hall, not a box.
Send it to my phone, please. I want to show Kathy without making her dig through albums.
Sent. Also, Sunday at 7 your time still works. The figs finally have leaves, so I can take you outside if the rain quits.
I got the picture. Tell Marco the frame from 2015 is still on the piano.
The figs are finally showing green. Did anything interesting come to your feeder this morning?
Two cardinals and the bossy little nuthatch. I wrote them on the pad by the sink before I lost count.
That pad is more organized than my whole garden notebook. Are you still working through the book with the Maine midwife?
Yes, but only after supper. The gray wool is already in my chair, so I may not get many pages.
I will be up at noon tomorrow. I can bring salad if you have the main part handled.
That will help. I have the crust chilling and the chicken cut small enough.
Good. Please leave the heavy dish for me to lift out if it is still hot.
I will. I also kept the magazine page flat so you cannot blame the creases this time.
Mom, Sophie wants old family photos for the shower table. Is the one with you in the pink blouse from Charleston?
Yes, near the Battery. Your father kept saying the sidewalks were not made for my shoes.
There is a little note on the back: hotel settled before leaving Saline. That is very Dad.
He liked knowing we would come home to our own bills and no extra surprises.
For tonight's call, do you want me to use the laptop instead of my phone? Last week the little Portland garden tour got muddy on your left side.
Laptop would help. I have the left piece in the charger now, and I will be at the kitchen table where the lamp is better.
Good. And no rushing after dark for anything I mention; photos can wait until tomorrow.
That is my rule anyway. Once the headlights start bouncing, I am home for the night.
On the call tonight, remind me to ask whether you found the Vanguard packet. Sometimes it hides under the church envelopes.
I found it. The Chase papers are clipped behind it, and the Bank of Ann Arbor page is in the blue folder.
Good. Is that all going to Richard in Ann Arbor this week?
Yes. I wrote the $250 check and put a sticky note on the 1988 folder so I remember which old copy he asked about.
Good morning. Before church, please remember the kitchen-counter row at 7:15, especially the 20 mg one.
I have the cup of water waiting. The little aspirin is already beside the D and calcium.
Thank you. I will stop worrying now. I will be up at noon with salad.
All done, right on time. See you at lunch.
I found the CDC page Dr. Nguyen mentioned. I can print it before Sunday lunch if your printer is still acting up.
Please do. I want to compare it with the yellow card before I put anything new on the kitchen calendar.
Good. Also, the Consumer Reports piece says the pharmacy forms should list the lot numbers, so bring those too.
They are in the blue folder with the Medicare papers. I will keep it by my purse.
I put the Harrington Heating receipt in the blue folder by your desk. The total still says 380.
Thank you. I want that paper with the January pages before I close March.
That makes sense. Did the gas bill come in lower yet, or is it still at the February level?
Still winter-sized. I left the quilt fabric envelope alone another month.
Are you taping Kristen this morning, or watching before church?
Before church. I have my coffee and puzzle out already, and I will still have time to put the roast in.
Good. Margaret may have the Senate guest afterward... worth hearing before Pat starts in on Tuesday.
I will catch that one too, then leave at nine. I like having the morning settled.
Pat says she is bringing that four-handed deck Tuesday... apparently she has been practicing the left bower.
Then she may finally stop ordering up when she ought to pass.
Also, Mr. Avery asked whether you might sit with him at Benny's after church next Sunday.
You know my answer. I will be home setting the table before six.
I am bringing Lily up next month. Do you want me to make those lemon bars she likes, or would that be too much sitting around the kitchen?
Maybe just half a pan. I have been better when dessert is one square of dark chocolate and then I close the drawer.
Half pan it is. I can bring chicken soup too, if that helps with lunches.
That would be useful. Salad at noon, soup the next day, and I will put the little monitor on after church if Kathy remembers the tape.
Walk still good at 8? I emailed you the library detour map last night.
Still walking at 8? Roads look clear by the library.
Yes. I already brushed the salt off the CR-V mats, so I will drive over and meet you near the book drop.
Yes. I saw it in Gmail with my toast. I wrote Maple to Harris on the slip by my keys.
Perfect. Bring water, that stretch is sloppy.
ty. Dave said the tire-pressure light went on in ours again. Yours behaving?
Already by the door. I looked at the map once more so I do not turn us the long way.
So far. I keep the service envelope with the title papers and receipts in the glove box, which makes Tony at the garage laugh.
Tree crew just blocked Maple by the library. Want to do the shorter loop at 10 instead?
That moves my whole morning around, but yes. I am trying to practice saying yes before I sharpen my pencil.
10 works. I'll bring water. ty for being flexible.
If we are done by quarter of three, I can still put the kettle on and sit where the light comes in.
I put the PBS clip aside for after cards tomorrow. Pat does not need an opening before the first hand...
Bless you. Ruth can tell us about the library book sale and we can keep the table civilized.
Good. Also, if Daniel sends you another march photo, save it for me. Marco's sign last time was excellent.
I will. You and I can look after the last rubber, when Pat is packing up.
Mom, did the Saline office ever fix your chart? You said the new portal still had you at 5-5.
Yes, I wrote it on the paper for Dr. Nguyen's nurse. 5-3 now, and about 140 with my shoes off.
Good. And did they give you the May card before Kathy starts arranging rides?
Not yet. They said the reminder should come after April 1, same place as last year.
Pat says the asparagus man is coming back downtown in June... I told her you would know before I would.
I keep the little cash pouch in the same drawer. It gets used up faster once those tables are back.
Of course it does. Good tomatoes are not a bargain, merely a necessity.
That is why I wrote $350 at the top of March and left myself a margin.
How did the Washtenaw call go? Marco says you should absolutely take the seat if they will let you sit in.
They were kind. I may start with the evening numbers class. Sister Mary Agnes would laugh to see me sharpening pencils again.
The nun with the red pencil?
The very one. In 1960 she wrote that I should keep my eye on ledgers, and I kept my eye on your father instead.
Ruth says the center has new coffee cups, so perhaps Tuesday bridge will survive after all...
Good. I was there this morning anyway, putting Linda's folder back after the bank screen finally matched.
You still have the patience you had with that mysterious forty dollars years ago.
It was only two digits turned around. I remember because I skipped lunch and then forgot why I had gone in.
Morning check-in from Portland. Did yesterday's grid go any better than the one with all the opera clues?
Finished it before breakfast. The opera one is still waiting for your sister to look smug over it.
She has earned the smugness if she can solve those. Are you making the flaky-top version this weekend or the beef one?
Beef this time, unless the butcher counter looks pitiful.
Mom, Jacob says his Portland school has the robotics showcase on March 27, so I may miss the first few minutes of our Sunday call that week.
Robotics comes first. I can wait and look at your garden when you are home.
Also, Brian texted from Denver about that laptop question. He says Emma's nursing schedule at Grand Valley sounds worse than his first year coding.
Those two always compare workloads. Tell Jacob I still have his birthday card on the piano.
I was thinking about you this week. Last year around this time you were waiting on that lab postcard after Dr. Levin took the small thing off your back.
Did the broker call go okay? Marco said to make sure you keep pictures of both cards in your phone, just in case.
I remember. Kathy kept me from fussing with the bandage, and then the postcard came and I put it in the blue medical folder.
It went fine. Same setup for this year. The two drafts together are just under $400, counting the pharmacy one.
That sounds steady at least. Is March still one of your normal months?
Good. And when Harold's date comes around, please let Kathy or Marjorie sit with you if mornings get too heavy again.
Yes. Groceries are about $350, utilities $220 if we don't get another cold snap, and gas for the car hardly moves past $40.
I will. I also took Linda's card from the senior center desk, just in case a quiet talk there would help.
Cold pavement today. Want to shorten to the library loop and skip the hill?
Yes, two miles is wiser. I took two extra-strength tablets with breakfast, so I should loosen up once we get moving.
Path behind the library looks salted but patchy. Want to skip 8?
I'll bring the thermos. Heating pad and that spicy tea after?
Let us skip. The driveway is cleared but the sidewalk still has shine at the curb.
That is the plan. Nothing from those little tins people keep recommending.
np. Rob came early then?
Yes, and I am staying on the porch unless I have the black-handled one with me.
Library path is clear except the puddle by the maple on Harris. Mill Pond path has cups near the bench again.
I'll bring a grocery sack on my way around. It is only four blocks, and I hate seeing that stuff blow toward the water.
ty. Monday we can start behind the library and loop back. I'll bring water.
Still walking at 8? Cooper already ate one glove.
Yes. I have to shake the gray hair off my black coat first. Winston slept against it all night on Harold's pillow.
Trade you for one muddy leash.
Good. If Saturday stays mild I may walk over with the book bag instead of bothering Kathy for a ride.
No thank you. Mine only steals quilt thread and judges me from the frame.
Route was icy by the library. Also, Cooper barked at your back fence like he saw royalty.
Probably the red-bellied one on the maple. He has been coming right after the walk.
Dave is looking at that boat out of Munising. You once told me the spray can soak your whole left side, right?
It can. Sit on the right going out if you want to keep your sweater decent.
ty for the warning. Don't forget your library bag tonight if you want me to drop it near the porch.
Mailbox was still icy when I passed. Want me to drop anything at the blue box on my way to work?
If you have room, yes. One for Sophie and one for Dolores, both sealed.
ty. He is trying to book before the early price changes.
np. Leave them inside the storm door. Also don't forget your 9 tomorrow if you still do that one.
I put it by the hall table with the burgundy skein so I will see both after dinner.
I do. I set the paper beside the phone so I am not hunting for it.
Harold always waited until the little jar matched the brochure number, but booking early did help once.
Storm looks like it will hit around 6. Want me to grab your mail before I go in?
Thank you, but I already brought it in. Soup is on and I am sitting down when the hour turns.
Figured. Cooper and I will stay out of your 6 pm chair time. ty
I can bring up the spare pillowcases Sunday. Did Rebecca take the cranberry dish back with her?
She forgot it, so I put it in the hall closet with the bag for April 4.
Good. I will wash the flannel sheets too. Emma may not need them in May, but they still have the holiday box smell.
Thank you. Leave the blue quilt alone, she likes that one.
Daniel's picture came through sharp on my screen. Dad in that Tigers cap made me smile.
He sent it right to my messages. I still remember how hot that June sidewalk was.
Did you want me to print it when I come Sunday at noon?
Yes, and remind me to charge the phone before 7. Daniel gets disappointed if the picture freezes when he is showing plants.
Did you and Eleanor get caught in that wind behind the library this morning?
Only on the last stretch. We stopped at two today and I was glad of it.
Sensible. My knees vote for two over three as well...
Eleanor teased that Cooper would have dragged us farther if he were along.
Marco asked what you want copied before we mail the USB. I have Keep on the Sunny Side, Little Moses, and the one with the flower in the title.
Those three are plenty. They sound right while I peel potatoes.
I also found that museum page with the open window and thin curtain. It reminded me of the picture over your sewing table.
Send it along. Quiet rooms are harder to get right than busy ones.
I can grab milk for you after rounds if the roads are slick.
Thank you, but I am already dressed. I will be at Busch's when the doors have settled down.
np. Text if the bags are too much and I'll run them up.
I am keeping it lighter this week. $92.40 left after today if I stick to the list.
I will be up at noon Sunday. Do you want me to carry the foil pan from the basement freezer before we leave?
Please. It is marked 3/7, chicken rice. I will have the sign-up sheet and pencils in my handbag.
All right. I can also bring the bank envelope if you want it on the front seat where you can see it.
That would help. I have twenty-nine entries this month already and do not want that envelope under the casserole dish.
Sarah asked whether the little lemon cakes would keep until Tuesday. Jim has a hospital call at two, so they may be closer to three-fifteen.
Three-fifteen is all right. I will set out the cups after lunch and not fuss over the exact minute.
That is progress... I will tell her the kettle will forgive them.
For bridge Tuesday, Pat is threatening to bring frosted cookies again...
Tell her I will admire them and take one home for the freezer. I will bring almonds and the small dark squares.
Sensible. Also, did your 6.8 number keep Dr. Patel from fussing?
Mostly. He only asked whether I was still doing the extra 5 mg from last summer and keeping the arm patch on schedule.
Pat says bridge may run long Tuesday... I told her some of us have a box score to check.
If the boys in Lakeland are tied in the ninth, I will be useless at cards.
And if the maize-and-blue women get the late slot again, we will both be yawning at choir.
I put fresh batteries in the little radio. Priorities.
Do you want me to stop by Chase on my way up tomorrow, or is that little certificate slip already copied?
Already copied. I only need a stamp for Richard's envelope and maybe a larger clip for the Bank of Ann Arbor sheet.
Okay. I can bring stamps. Did the monthly $200 transfer land yet?
It came through after the federal check and Harold's retirement payment. I wrote it on the yellow pad.
Kathy said you found my graduation program in the house papers. I forgot you kept that.
Harold put it with the bank envelope that summer. He said it was a good year twice over.
That sounds like Dad. Please don't climb for the top shelf next time, okay? I'll reach it when I come up.
I used the step stool and only needed the folder for Kathy's latest idea about making life easier.
Marco opened a red for dinner and I thought of you saving the same bottle from Thanksgiving to Christmas.
Before our call tomorrow, do you want me to look at that 2026 workbook again? I can help make the April and May lines less jumpy.
It is still in the pantry with the little rubber stopper. I only poured the one glass when everyone was here.
Maybe. April has the car one, May has the house one for 1400, and then July starts the tax bother.
That sounds exactly right. Did Kathy send the PBS NewsHour segment about the spring recommendations?
We can smooth it out without changing your gift lines. You were pretty clear about 600 in December and 400 spread over birthdays.
Yes. I watched it after supper and put a note to ask Dr. Nguyen whether my 2023 line is enough for now.
Those stay. The fabric can wait until the savings line is back where I like it.
I put the serving bowl back in the china cabinet, second shelf. The one with the tiny crack is wrapped in a dish towel.
Thank you. I will use the smaller blue plate tonight. It is only me, but I still like it done properly.
Tom found Dad's old score pad in the drawer with the pencils. Do you want me to bring it Sunday?
Yes. Your father kept the neatest columns, even when he stole the deal.
Did you survive the small people and the leprechaun books this morning?
Barely. Sixteen of them, and one boy wanted the green glitter everywhere. I was glad I only stayed until noon.
Two hours is enough. Four was too much, especially after walking home with that canvas bag.
The walk was the best part. I cut past Mill Pond and picked up two napkins before they reached the ducks.
Did you ever find the folder from when you changed cars? I am trying to make myself file my own papers before they become archaeology...
I did. Harold had clipped the certified check stub to the old Accord trade sheet, neat as anything.
Of course he did. Ken would have put it under fishing licenses.
The 2019 paperwork is all together now. I put the card statement receipt in the same cabinet while I was standing there.
Marco and I are leaving at 7 for the courthouse steps. I will send photos if the rain lets up.
Send them after my call with Marjorie. She still laughs about the cardboard fish you carried in Portland.
Deal. And for November, are we still doing the table rule from 2016? I do not want Greg and me staring each other down over pie.
Yes. Rebecca relaxes when everyone sticks to weather, kids, and food.
I will be up at noon. Do you need me to bring anything besides the salad?
No, thank you. I already have the chicken thawing, carrots from the freezer, and the rosemary and thyme I dried from the south bed.
That sounds like Sunday at your house. Tom also asked whether the apple pan is making an appearance.
Only if those orchard slices soften before church lets out. The crust is resting under the towel.
I am stopping at the post office before lunch. Did that Missouri Star package ever arrive, or should I check the porch?
It came yesterday. The red print is darker than it looked online, but it will work for the border.
Good. Please do not try to finish the whole border today. Your hands were bothering you last Sunday.
I set the kitchen timer for an hour and a half. After that I can wind the green yarn instead.
I saved us the second pew on the aisle. Pastor Jim faces that way when he reads the announcements, which should be kinder to your left side.
Thank you. I put in fresh batteries before breakfast, so I should catch more than last Sunday.
Good. I can drive to Mac's afterward if fellowship runs long. The clouds are making everything look flat.
Yes, please. I do better making my own way when it is bright and plain.
If bridge runs long tomorrow, I can still drop you near IHA afterward. My library returns can wait.
Thank you, but Kathy has the folder from Dr. Nguyen already. It is just the May scheduling slip and the old comparison dates.
Ah. The annual errand. I remember Ken's folders multiplying like rabbits after 2005.
Mine is thinner now, thank heavens. I only keep what the Saline office asks for.
Mom, did the insurance email for Lily's appointment come through? I sent it to your Gmail around lunch.
I will look after supper. I am still matching the numbers from the electric page to my little book.
Okay. No rush. Just wanted you to have it before I forget.
I copied 86.42 twice before I closed the page. I will answer you when I open mail.
Still good for 8 behind the library? Pavement may be wet. Bring water.
Yes. I just need my 7:15 kitchen stop first, then shoes.
np. I can wait by the bench if you run late.
Done. The little white 20 and the four morning extras are crossed off.
Dave booked Traverse City for May 18-21. Could Cooper stay with you those nights?
Yes. Put his food scoop and pills in the usual tote.
Ty. That makes four trips this year if July happens too. Also, Mon at 8 is still good?
Good. Same rear lot unless the repaving signs are still up.
Are you still going to the lower room tonight? I found two cream scraps in the church closet that may suit your star corners.
Tonight is only the third Thursday, so no. I will save my hands for the 26th.
Then I will put them in my choir folder for Sunday. Also, I saw a PBS piece on the Paducah riverfront exhibit... you would enjoy the old stitching frames.
I marked that one to watch after supper. The town keeps landing on my someday list.
Kathy texted me the brochure for the Maple Road place. I told her I'd ask you gently, not gang up.
She means well. But the tomatoes already have their stakes, and your father's oak is leafing early.
I remember that oak barely taller than me. If I come in July, I'll help with the beds before it gets hot.
Good. This old Michigan Avenue place still knows where everyone belongs.
I can bring the Ann Arbor library puzzle book on Sunday. Tom is making soup, so I will bring a container up with me.
Good. Remind me to show you the note from Emma about her clinical rotation.
I would like that. Did Rebecca ever send the photo of Sophie trying on the plain gold band?
Yes, and I printed one for the refrigerator. Rebecca said Toledo traffic was awful when they went.
Mom, Caleb can scan those workshop papers when we come up in April. He has a fast scanner at Bowling Green.
That would help. I only need the years 1966 through 1992, especially the little slips where men paid for mower and snowblower work.
Do you want the old school envelope scanned too? The one from Sister Mary Agnes?
Yes. Put it with the WCC papers. I want to see if they still believe a woman my age can finish what she set down.
Lily asked if the Humane Society picture is still on your fridge. The little gray face in the 2020 folder.
It is still there, though the little face is not little anymore. The clinic scale said just over sixteen.
That explains why he makes the bed dip on Dad's side. 🙂
Every night. I keep Harold's extra pillow there and Winston takes the warm spot.
Marco found your bracket note tucked in the recipe photo. You really did circle Ann Arbor all the way to the second weekend.
I also wrote 4-2 on the kitchen calendar for the road opener, so my loyalties are organized if nothing else.
That sounds exactly like you. Should I call after the last out or after the final buzzer?
After whichever one lets me breathe first.
I found Dad's old TV guide clipping in the pie safe. It has Stagecoach circled for Saturday night.
Your father knew I would stay awake for that one.
There is also a postcard of a white farmhouse in snow tucked behind it. Do you want me to bring both on April 4?
Yes. Put them in the blue folder so they don't bend.
Your tomato notes made me laugh. Mine are still under lights, and Marco says I am fussing over them like infants.
Marco found a stack of tiny seed packets for kids. Want me to mail them for your Saturday bag?
Tell Marco I put May through October on the paper calendar: 7 to 8 outside, then no one is allowed to call until I wash up.
Yes, but nothing fussy. They like shaking things more than planting them. Maybe beans in paper cups.
Fair. Save me the carrot and herb instructions before July, please. He wants to try the top crust again.
I will write it out. Remind him the cabbage patch has to earn its place first, or there will be no jars for the basement shelf.
Paper cups, got it. No plastic. Your rules are rubbing off on us.
Good. If children can carry home a bean and not a plastic trinket, I count that as a decent morning.
Greg's cousin asked if you wanted the extra patio ashtray for the garage sale box. I told him I had never seen one at your house. 🙂
No need for it here. Put it with his camping things if he wants to keep it.
Also, I found your March 2021 and April 2021 pharmacy copies in the Toledo folder by mistake. I will bring them May 2.
Thank you. Kathy is helping me get all those loose papers clipped behind the yellow card.
Mom, Lily said your blue bubbles are working again. She wants to send you her track photo after dinner.
Good. I had Daniel help me last Sunday when my little camera button vanished.
Before your 7 o'clock with them tonight, plug it in. Marco sent me the dahlia picture and it used half my battery just opening it.
It is plugged in now. I am ready for the garden tour.
Can I call for two minutes, or are you with Amna and Geoff?
Let me call you after supper. I just sat down with my plate.
No rush. I saw the Sunday clip you mentioned too; Marco said the roundtable was better than the headline.
Tell Marco I agree. I will ring at seven, before I start getting ready for bed.
Route behind the library is clear now. Want to do the short loop Thurs at 8? I can stand on your right if the wind is loud.
Short loop sounds right. I will bring the small case; the left one pops loose when I wear the knit hat.
np. Also I can grab milk on my way home today if you skipped Busch's because of the late rain.
I did skip it. I will go tomorrow morning when the streets look sharper.
I am stopping at the post office before bridge. Do you need stamps, or are you still stocked?
A small book would help. I used three since Saturday and have Dolores's December note draft tucked in my address book already.
You are admirably steady with paper and ink. I will bring the stamps to the senior center.
Thank you. I have to be home Friday by nine, but Tuesday bridge is safe.
Pat says she may bring a jar of something her niece swears by for stiff hands. I told her not to start a sales table at bridge...
Please do. I am sticking with the ginger tea, the heating pad, walking, and two Tylenol when the knees complain.
Sensible. I remember you saying no to your nephew's 2020 suggestion too.
Exactly. I have enough to keep track of with the BP pill.
For May 2, can we keep lunch like Thanksgiving rules? Greg is already grumbling about Daniel's courthouse pictures.

events.title: Daniel + M

events.title: Coffee, oatmeal, reading, puzzle
events.notes: Leave enough time before 8:00 walk. Turn on Channel 56 at 6:00 tonight before supper gets cold.

events.title: Library loop with Eleanor
events.notes: Bring water. Two-mile route. Heat pad afterward if the right side is cranky; extra-strength Tylenol, 2 tablets, only if needed.

events.title: Library back lot - E.
events.notes: Blue bottle; shorter route. Ask about Cooper key before her early call.

events.title: Rob - driveway if overnight glaze sticks
events.notes: $40 cash in blue mug by side door. Put black-handled stick by kitchen steps before getting paper.

events.title: Seed trays and pantry shelf
events.notes: Check tomato flats, carrot tape, cabbage packets, rosemary and thyme starts. Count quart jars on lower shelf; two left from last crock. Move orchard apple bags to kitchen freezer.

events.title: CVS pickup before oatmeal
events.notes: 90-day refill ready; check whether the reader strips and arm patches are in the Medicare bag. Breakfast after: oats, berries, coffee.

events.title: Morning pillbox
events.notes: Tuesday slot: 20 mg tablet plus multi, D, calcium, and tiny aspirin before oatmeal.

events.title: DTE and water: screen totals + blue spiral
events.notes: Open Gmail after breakfast first. Pencil dates in left margin before entering anything.

events.title: Call Maggie
events.notes: Adrian paper page open; finish Lily's envelope before mailbox pickup.

events.title: Enter February house numbers
events.notes: Gas 250 again. Add April auto premium reminder. Check second 190 transfer back to savings line after March statement.

events.title: Center March packet for Linda
events.notes: QBO bank feed, grant tabs, February receipts, board pages by 4:00. Check old file note on the $40 transposed entry before sending.

events.title: Kathy driving - Derm check + senior center desk

events.notes: Ask Dr. Levin to glance at the little back scar from last March. Bring the two empty November bottles to ask pharmacy bin rules later. Stop at senior center front desk for Linda's open-hour card.

events.title: Sort blue ferry folder before Kathy comes
events.notes: Keep the Mackinac postcards and Harold's pencil totals. Put motel receipt copies in the small envelope.

events.title: Pick up tiny batteries before bridge
events.location: CVS, E Michigan Ave, then Saline Senior Center
events.notes: Use the front table if Ruth gets there first. Leave by 4:15 so Michigan Ave is still easy.

events.title: Cards - Saline Senior Center
events.notes: Bring lemon squares. Sit across from M. If Pat starts on cable-news talk, ask Ruth about her grandson's robotics meet.

events.title: Set table; six o'clock plate; cards after

events.title: Blue yarn, Chapter 9
events.notes: Set feeder tray by kitchen window first; check suet block before dark.

events.title: Nguyen office: yearly form update

events.title: Sort March folder for R. Beauchamp

events.title: Kettle, blue cup, east windows

events.title: Visa statement amount from checking
events.notes: Use March statement number only; file receipt in blue folder with county tax and CR-V title papers.

events.title: Call WCC senior audit desk
events.notes: Ask about ACC 111 seat availability, prior credits from 1959-60, and whether old ledgers can count for placement. Have Harold 1099 folder nearby.

events.title: Busch's list + receipts

events.title: Dr. Nguyen - bring yellow card

events.title: Call HAP broker - keep same blue lettered plan?

events.title: Make two pans of chicken rice

events.title: Rebecca up from Toledo

events.title: Sunday lunch moved early; TV on after dishes

events.title: Sunday disc and sketchbook night

events.title: Video: Daniel and Marco

events.title: Winston yearly check

events.title: Find blue house folder for Kathy
